newsitem.title: USA: US bankers hail Fed proposal to ease restrictions.
newsitem.headline: US bankers hail Fed proposal to ease restrictions.

text.p: The ABA Securities Association on Wednesday praised a proposal by the Federal Reserve to remove barriers that limit banks' activities in the securities industry.
The group, an affiliate of the American Bankers Association, called the proposal a bold step that would make it easier for banks to compete in the industry.

"The Fed has scored a regulatory hat-trick today by proposing to lift anachronistic rules that have long outlived their usefulness," Larry LaRocco, managing director of the association said in a statement.
"These changes recognize how dramatically the marketplace has changed since the firewalls were adopted nine years ago," LaRocco added.

Earlier on Wednesday, the Fed voted to consider a proposal that would ease a number of barriers, or "firewalls," that separate activities of bank holding companies and their investment-banking affiliates.

In 1987, the Fed first allowed bank affiliates to engage in underwriting activities, subject to restrictions on the proportion of revenue they could derive from the business and to a number of other restrictions.
The proposal up for consideration would remove many of the remaining firewalls. The proposal was submitted for a 60-day comment period.
